evidence_chunks: Music Music has been my primary creative outlet throughout my life. I was classically trained as a percussionist, later transitioning to guitar and songwriting in my twenties. Over the years, I’ve performed with several local bands, including Scratched Vinyl, Strumpet, We The Band, and most recently Great Highway. My musical style has evolved across genres, ranging from rock and acoustic jazz to blues, and more recently, electronic rock. With Great Highway, I’ve contributed to over five full-length albums, in addition to appearing on three other albums with previous projects. Great Highway is an eclectic, high-energy dance-rock group often described as indietronica. Their sound blends electric harp, alto saxophone, drums, and layered synth textures to create emotionally resonant, earworm-driven songs. Music provides a sense of calm and mental clarity for me, and it has always gone hand in hand with my creative scientific pursuits. These days, one of my favorite ways to unwind at home is by playing simple classical guitar pieces on my nylon- string guitar.

and creative writing with AI-generated illustrations, voice transcription, story-to-play script conversion, and real-

visualizations (Python, TensorFlow, and Streamlit). 98% precision for finding tumors. https://bit.ly/BTDetect 
• Designed and built a pharmacogenomic platform to match cancer patients with personalized therapies by 
analyzing tumor genetics and drug responses. Discovered treatments for patients that failed standard of care and 
led to the development of five novel clinical trial concepts (Python, MySQL, AWS, and Tableau). PMID:37440745

Directed IND-enabling studies internally and with CROs in multiple mouse tumor models, including CDX, 
PDX, and humanized mouse models for exploring ADCs and immunotherapy. Developed in vivo models, 
dosing protocols, and additional processes for analysis of protein and mRNA-based biologics.  
• 
Drove discovery of biomarkers leading to their development and implementation in Phase I clinical trials. 
• 
Provided strategic input for multiple projects as a member of the research leadership team and worked 
effectively across departments to meet critical timelines. 
• 
Prepared non-clinical pharmacology reports for the CX-801 and CX-2051 IND submissions. 
• 
As IACUC Chair, oversaw the management of an on-site animal care facility, administration of all IACUC 
protocols, and was responsible for AAALAC accreditation.  
• 
Demonstrated ability to analyze, navigate, and troubleshoot project issues in a fast-paced environment, 
leading team in researching multiple oncology and non-oncology targets. 
 
California Pacific Medical Center Research Institute (CPMCRI). San Francisco, CA 
- 
 A research institute affiliated with Sutter Health with a focus on oncology. 
Senior Scientist, Cancer Avatar Project   
 
 
 
 
 
 
(2016-2021) 
Executed strategic development and leadership of the Cancer Avatar Project, a precision medicine program in 
support of determining therapeutic solutions in fully individualized patient cancer care. Led cross-functional 
teams in the utilization of a multimodal approach, including developing a library of PDX mouse models with 
corresponding genomics, high-throughput drug screens, and informatics. Oversaw day-to-day operations of the 
program, leading the implementation of integrated project plans and timelines. 
• 
Collaborated with programmers, physicians, and bioinformatics specialists in developing a 
pharmacogenomic platform, aligning HTDS, DNA, and RNA sequencing data from patient tumors with 
corresponding PDX mouse models.   
• 
Managed experiments for preclinical evaluation of drug efficacy, PK, PD, and assessment of drug 
combination interactions.   
• 
Directed project communications across all team members and collaborators. Developed detailed 
presentations for the executive team, investors, donors, and industry partners such as Amgen, GW 
Pharmaceutical, Organix Inc, and Oregon Health & Science, delivering consistent, up-to-date information on 
project activities and status.  
• 
Drove development of multiple preclinical projects to discover drug combinations in the treatment of 
immunotherapy-resistant metastatic melanoma and recurrent glioblastoma, resulting in the initiation of 
clinical trials.  
• 
Successfully co-developed and awarded multiple extramural grants as well as industry contracts. 
 
Scientist, Avrygen Therapeutics   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
(2012-2016) 
- 
A company developing next-generation nanoparticle delivery technologies. 
As part of a biotech incubator space initiative at CPMCRI, supported Avrygen Therapeutics leveraging strong 
analytical abilities in the design, development, and optimization of in vitro and in vivo models to analyze next-
generation nanoparticle delivery technologies for delivery of miRNA, siRNA, and DNA.    
• 
Utilized expertise to implement in vitro assays in the determination of effectiveness of novel microsphere 
formulation for long-term butyrylcholinesterase delivery. 
• 
Communicated clear milestones, goals, timeframes, and resource planning as project leader, in 
alignment with project objectives. 
• 
Presented compelling pitches to investors and co-developed eight grants supporting project execution.  
• 
Developed research and evaluation techniques for preclinical analysis of nanoparticle delivery systems 
aimed at various applications, including treating drug addiction and targeting tumor-driving proteins in breast 
and brain cancer models. 
 
Scientist, Development of Cannabinoid-based Therapeutics   
 
 
 
(2011-2016) 
Leader in the field of research investigating cannabinoids in the treatment of aggressive cancers, including 
breast cancer, glioblastoma, and head and neck cancer. Preclinical discoveries promoted academia and 
industry collaboration in the development of novel cannabinoid-based inhibitors of cancer, leading to multiple 
clinical trials. Additional cannabinoid-therapeutic evaluations included the development of inhibitors of 
neuropathic pain and neurodegenerative disease and the synthesis of cannabinoid-based weight loss drugs.   
• 
Discovered the cannabinoid cannabidiol represents the first small molecule inhibitor of Id proteins, which 
play a key role in the invasive and metastatic progression of multiple cancers, leading to multiple clinical 
trials targeting glioblastoma.   
• 
Discovered CBD inhibits neuropathic pain in chemotherapy-induced and spinal cord injury-induced 
neuropathic pain models.  
• 
Collaborated on the discovery of the effectiveness of cannabinoids to delay the onset of ALS in a genetic 
mouse model, leading to a small pilot clinical trial resulting in positive outcomes. 
• 
Utilized a combination of biomolecular computer modeling and site-directed mutagenesis of GPCRs to 
create second-generation cannabinoid receptor antagonists for the development of non-stimulant weight 
loss therapies.
